card.name: Point where a caution or monitoring instruction begins
card.fires_on: The word or comma that ends a condition clause (a drug combination or patient group) right before an instruction to take care, monitor or observe. It fires in drug-interaction and warning text.

modes.label: Comma after condition
modes.description: A comma closing an 'if/when used with' clause, just before a monitoring instruction.
modes.example: When such drugs are administered to a patient receiving INVOKAMET or INVOKAMET XR<<,>> monitor for loss of blood glucose control.

modes.label: Care wording
modes.description: The verb right before or within a 'care must be taken' or 'requires great caution' phrase.
modes.example: When metolazone tablets, USP, are used with other antihypertensive drugs, care must be<< taken>>, especially during initial therapy.

modes.label: Noun ending a clause
modes.description: A noun such as therapy or patients that closes the clause before an instruction.
modes.example: Adjust dosing of insulin or other anti-diabetic<< therapy>> accordingly.

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words meaning 'be careful', 'pay attention', 'in time' and 'lest'.
card.plain: It marks the spot in a warning where the text is about to tell the reader to be careful or watch the patient.
